Nothing open touches either. Re-verify at your claim.

## The defect, and why it is the sharpest one left

A row action declaring `recordIdField` receives `undefined` for it, because the grid never projects that column. `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` reads `rowRecord[action.recordIdField]` — a correct generic read — but the grid builds `$select` from **listView columns + `id` + predicate fields only**. `recordIdField` is not harvested.

Measured instance: `sys_session` declares `revoke_session` with `recordIdField: 'token'`, and `token` is in **no** listView. So the action sends no token, better-auth's `revoke-session` matches nothing, deletes nothing — **and still answers `{ status: true }`.**

**"Revoke Session" reports success and revokes nothing.** A security control that silently no-ops while claiming to have worked.

## ⛔ Premise check first — the end-to-end was NEVER run

The card is explicit and this is binding: the projection gap is **read from code**; nobody has clicked Revoke Session and observed nothing revoked. **Reproduce before fixing.** If the behaviour has changed, `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is a complete delivery.

Also: line anchors are from 2026-08-12 and **will** have moved. Take them from the tree. Four cards today had stale bodies that changed the work — assume this one does too until you have checked.

## ⛔ The live interaction — read this before choosing a fix

`objectstack-ai/objectstack#7823` proposes `internal: true` on `sys_session.token`. **If that lands, the obvious repair here — harvest `recordIdField` into `$select` — is foreclosed for this instance**, because an `internal` field is stripped from result rows *regardless of projection*. That card is a **design exit still awaiting a maintainer ruling**, so the interaction is live, not hypothetical.

**How to scope around it:** fix the **general** defect — any `recordIdField` outside the listView is silently `undefined` — which is correct no matter how #7823 is ruled. ⛔ Do **not** build a special case for `sys_session.revoke_session`, and ⛔ do not assume either card's outcome. If your fix cannot be written without depending on #7823's outcome, **stop and report** — that is a genuine fork.

## Zone 2 — scope, stated because the card separates two things

1. **The general projection gap is yours.** The card warns: enumerate the *other* `recordIdField` declarations rather than fixing the one that surfaced it — a per-action patch leaves the class open. Report what the enumeration found.
2. **The silent success is NOT yours.** An action that identifies no record answering `{ status: true }` is **server-side**, in `objectstack`. The moved card says so explicitly. If you think it needs fixing, that is a card in the other repo — ⛔ do not reach for it.

## Tests

Pin the general property: an action whose `recordIdField` is **not** a listView column still receives a defined value. And pin the negative that makes it meaningful — before the fix, that same case yields `undefined`. A test that only exercises a `recordIdField` which happens to already be a column proves nothing.

## Gates

Derive from your diff — expect `Lint`, `Type Check`, the shards, changeset gates, `Control Byte Scan`. Changeset required (`@object-ui/plugin-grid`, and `@object-ui/core` if `predicate-fields.ts` moves). Score `minor` at most; ⛔ never `major`.

⛔ **Do not background a long check and end your turn** — three devs hit that trap today. If a suite queues behind the shared verify lock, narrow it and **declare the narrowing**.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first line `Fixes #5217`. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report **and** post it as an issue comment whose first line is `<!-- os-dev-report -->`. Note this card was **moved from `objectstack-ai/objectstack#8018` today** — the original thread there has 5 comments that were not copied, and they are worth reading.

## Notes for the PM beyond the JSON

**Enumeration of `recordIdField` declarations — the card's deliverable #1, done across both repos.** `objectui` ships **zero** declarations: every hit in this repo is machinery (`ActionRunner`, `actionKeys`, `serverActionHandler`, `recordIdParam`) or a test fixture. `objectstack` ships **exactly one**: `sys_session.revoke_session` (`platform-objects/src/identity/sys-session.object.ts:67`, `recordIdField: 'token'` with `recordIdParam: 'token'`). Everything else there is the spec key itself, generated translation bundles, protocol plumbing, or a test fixture. So the class has **one live instance**, and it is the foreclosed one — which is exactly why the merged fix put the harvest in the shared helper and added a pre-dispatch refusal rather than patching an action.

**What the one live instance does today.** `sys_session.token` is `internal: true`, so it is stripped from result rows regardless of projection — `$select` now asks for `token` and the row still arrives without it. The row therefore hits the **refusal** path, not the false-success path: `useConsoleActionRuntime` calls `resolveRecordIdParamSeed` and returns `{ success: false, error }` **before** the request. The existing test at `useConsoleActionRuntime.test.tsx:920` pins precisely this with a fixture shaped identically to the real declaration (`recordIdParam: 'token'`, `recordIdField: 'token'`, and the `{ status: true }` response mocked), asserting `authFetchSpy` was **not** called. So "Revoke Session" no longer reports success while revoking nothing — it reports a refusal. The server still answers `{ status: true }` to any other caller, which is objectstack#9714.

**Why I was cleaning up, since it read as an abort:** it was the end of a falsification run, not a stop. `node_modules` was removed; the `git worktree remove` and the empty-branch deletion were both **blocked by the harness permission classifier**, so `/home/user/objectui-issue-5217` still exists (clean tree, no `node_modules`) and the empty remote branch is still pushed. Neither needs any action from me, but neither is mine to force.

**Recommendation:** close objectui#5217 as already-fixed by objectui#4670 + objectui#4678, rather than re-dispatching. If anything from this card is still wanted, it is objectstack#9714.
